exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: Reproductive-age women (15-49 years) in Nigeria who had at least one childbirth in the last 5 years prior to the 2018 survey (n=19,101)
finding: Women who underwent a Caesarean section had five times lower odds of TIBF compared to women who had a vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The negative effect of Caesarean section on TIBF can be partially mitigated by skin-to-skin contact.
